LESSON: LOG ROLL AND T-BALANCE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Performing and Display
Topic 2.4: Log Roll and T-Balance
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Log Roll and T-Balance, part of Performing and Display in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one CREATIVE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why should there be good spacing while performing log rolls and T balance?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify log roll and T- balance through practice,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Log Roll and T-Balance in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. make markers for use during log rolls and T- balance performance

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Log Roll and T-Balance in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. perform log roll for coordination,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Log Roll and T-Balance in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. perform T-balance for flexibility,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Log Roll and T-Balance in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate performing log roll and T-balance for enjoyment. ● Learners to watch a video clip or a demonstration of a log roll. Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. ● Learners to watch a video clip or demonstration of a T- balance. Screen resolution and light intensity could be regulated for learners who are sensitive to light. ● Learners to collect and share reusable materials for making markers to be used during the log roll and T- balance performance with peers. Safety precautions for all the learners should be observed with extra caution taken for learners with health conditions and those using mobility Why should there be good spacing while performing log rolls and T balance? 31 devices by ensuring that they move in a safe environment. ● Learners to work collaboratively to mark the open space using the improvised markers. Safety precautions for all the learners should be observed with extra caution taken for learners with health conditions and those using mobility devices by ensuring that they mark in safe environment ● Learners to perform log roll in different directions while observing safety. Learners with postural defects could use alternative functional parts of the body, perform an alternative corresponding activity, or perform at their level of functional ability ● Learners to perform T-balance with peers while observing safety. 32 ● Learners to sing action songs while performing log roll and T balance. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech, hum, mime or use alternative mode of communications. ● Leaners to talk/write/type positively about own and others performance in log roll and T – balance.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Log Roll and T-Balance together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and imagination: as the learner identifies simple reusable materials, and makes markers.

● Communication and Collaboration: as the learner talks about others performance in log rolls and T-balance,

Values:
● Love: is promoted as the learner shares simple reusable materials with peers.

● Respect: is nurtured as the learner portrays positive regard for self and others as they work in groups.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Health promotion issues: are enhanced the learner observes safety when collecting materials to be used in making markers.

● Environmental conservation: is promoted as the learner collects reusable materials.

Link to other learning areas:

● Environmental activities: as the learner observes hygiene while collecting and sharing simple reusable materials.

● Religious Activities: as the learner applies values while positively talking about others performance.

Suggested learning resources:
